description: Mobile School Pantry (MSP) mission is to provide nutritious, healthy food items to children and families at low-income schools in South Florida. We are committed to creating a future without hunger where all families have access to adequate amounts of nutritious, culturally appropriate foods to learn, grow and thrive. Everyone has the power to make an impact… It all starts with one action: Become a Hunger Hero by volunteering at one of Mobile School Pantry’s client choice school pantries. Offering client choice allows families to select their own food instead of receiving pre-packed bags. This process provides dignity for families, prevents food waste and ultimately saves money. Volunteer, donate and help our (growing) school pantry program. YOU make it all possible! Volunteers needed to assist with our client choice school pantry, tasks include: Unloading of truck Set-up client choice school pantry Refill baskets with produce items as needed throughout the giveaway Assist families to shop Breakdown boxes Clean-up post giveaway Smile and make families feel welcomed WE BELIEVE: Food Security for ALL Food is crucial for the well-being and success of all individuals and the foundation of a strong, vibrant society. HEALTHY, fresh food should be a human right YOU make the difference. Your time fuels our mission and helps us serve children and families in our community. We hope to see you soon! *Please wear comfortable clothing and closed-toed shoes Must be 14 years old to attend without an adult Please bring your ID and check in at the school office. Let them know you're there to volunteer with Mobile School Pantry. Just a friendly reminder that school campuses close at a specific time each day, so we truly appreciate your help in arriving on time for both drop‑off and pick‑up. Your punctuality keeps things running smoothly and ensures we can wrap up the day safely and comfortably. Thank you so much for your cooperation and support!

description: Catholic Hospice, serving Miami-Dade and Broward Counties, is looking for Companion Care Volunteers. Companion Care Volunteers provide companionship to hospice patients and respite to caregivers by playing games with a patient, reading, singing songs, or simply just spending time with them. Patient visits are available 7 days a week from 9 am till 9 pm throughout Miami-Dade and Broward county. As a volunteer with Catholic Hospice, you will receive specialized training in serving hospice patients and ongoing support to meet the specific needs of terminally ill patients living in their own homes, nursing homes, assisted living communities, and medical centers. Volunteering with hospice does not have to be sad; it can be a truly uplifting experience. Volunteering can be one of the most rewarding experiences you may ever have. Taking a few hours out of your week to spend time with a hospice patient can make a profound difference in their life and yours. After your initial contact expressing interest in this volunteer opportunity, I'll email you a volunteer application to be filled out. Requirements for all new volunteers are the following: submit to a drug screening, background screening, and TB (Tuberculosis) test, which is at the cost of Catholic Hospice. Additionally, potential volunteers must provide a copy of their Covid-19 vaccination card. If you're not vaccinated due to medical reasons, then a letter from your physician will allow you to be exempted from the requirement. Volunteer training is done once a month via zoom and you're expected to participate on one of the training dates. Once all requirements have been met, you're officially able to visit patients.

Submit your one-time LifeNet4Families volunteer application and waiver at www.lifenet4families.org (required before any shift).

Register and book your desired shift in HandsOn South Florida.

Confirm your booking
Check your HandsOn account or email for confirmation or  emails from lvaughn@ln4f.org. Shifts may be waitlisted or declined if schedules change, capacity is met, or a group booking supersedes an individual sign-up.

Meal prep, café service, station setup, plating, and maintaining a clean, welcoming environment.

Assemble food boxes, restock, rotate inventory, and support client flow with care and accuracy.

Clothing Attendant
Sort, size, and organize donations; maintain the clothing room; assist clients with appropriate attire.

Step 4: Eligibility & Youth

  • Volunteers age 16 must serve with a parent/guardian.

  • All volunteers must have an approved application and scheduled shift.

Group Volunteer Procedure (Mandatory)

To ensure capacity, safety, and a great client experience, all groups must follow the group process. Individual sign-ups submitted by members of a group will be declined and must be rescheduled under the official group workflow.

  • Student Volunteer Hours: Students are responsible for tracking their hours and bringing any school-required forms for signature at the end of their service.

  • Parking: Due to limited parking, carpooling is recommended. Park on the street or in front of the warehouse.

title: Support Girls in Your Community – Volunteer with Girl Scouts!
time_label: Ongoing
description: Do you want to make a difference in the lives of girls in your community? Girl Scouts of Southeast Florida is seeking dedicated volunteers to serve as Troop Leaders or Troop Helpers in Broward County! You’ll help girls grow into confident leaders through fun, hands-on activities in STEM, the outdoors, life skills, and entrepreneurship. No prior experience needed—just a positive attitude and a willingness to make a meaningful impact. We provide all training and materials! Roles Available: Troop Leader: Organize and lead regular troop meetings with the support of other volunteers and Girl Scout staff. Troop Helper: Assist with troop meetings, activities, and events as needed. Time Commitment: Flexible—most troops meet 2–4 times per month. We’ll work with your schedule! Perfect for College Students! We offer internship opportunities for students looking to gain experience working with youth while earning college credit or community service hours . Ideal for education, social work, psychology, or child development majors. Benefits: ✅ Flexible scheduling ✅ Training and resources provided ✅ Earn college credit or service hours ✅ Build your resume and leadership skills ✅ Make a difference in the lives of girls! Get Started: Click “Express Interest” or contact us at mberry@gssef.org / 561-850-9027 (text/call) to learn more and find a troop near you.
